files: workbench/recheck_order.py (new, item 1, lane B): 'What this change did', the read side only. change(kernel, principal, ident, before=None) sorts everything that stands on a changed sheet into three piles. Worked again: a calculation that reads a changed row, worked again exactly in memory with its own recipe; the card says whether its page already carries the new result. Needs you: a finding or plain page whose words still carry a number that moved (including results and cell values from before earlier changes), a check that reads a changed row or rows it cannot tell, or a calculation that cannot be worked. Carried over, with proof: 'reads rows 2 and 4, which did not change', 'its check reads row 5, which did not change; it rests on ...', or 'reads nothing of this sheet, and rests on ... which did not change'. It also gives each goal over the sheet (goals.candidates plus kept goals): its state and worst-case room before and now, judged by one in-memory judge() on both sides with the owner's tolerances held against each side's own cells. For each change of state it gives the cause, found by putting one changed cell back at a time. 'Before' is the sheet's last saved version from the Office's own office_history, or the caller's {cell: value}. Operation field.change {id: 'office:...' or a calculation 'document:...', before?} (read). Helpers that work alone: changed_rows, saved_versions, last_saved, put_back, work, judge, rows_words.

decisions: The design's 300 mA vector says 'four findings carried over'. I read this as four carried-over things: the startup power calculation (the design's own proof wording, 'reads rows 2 and 4', describes that calculation) plus the three other findings of the investigation that watches the sheet through its check on the readings sheet, following field_ripple's 'watches it' rule. The open question (a QUESTION claim) is not sorted.

'Before' defaults to the sheet's last saved version, read from the Office's own office_history table. No Office API exposes it, so this is a single SELECT through store().catalog.db(). A caller can pass before={cell: value} instead.

Goals are judged by a small in-memory judge() in recheck_order instead of an edit to goals.py, so a sheet with cells put back can be judged without being saved. It uses the same building blocks as goals.judge (goals._ways, tolerances.sheet_cell, math_answers.bindings_from_cells, answer('check')). Tolerance states are recomputed against each side's own cells (tolerances._all, tolerances.cell_state).
'Worst room' is per goal: the least room over the ways (Rev A, Rev B), reported only for goals whose room moved. 'Nothing changes state' is checked over the goals of the sheet.

Plain pages whose words carry a number that moved are also put under 'needs you' (Rail Demo's summary page says 250 mA and 3 W). This goes beyond the Field's own rule, which marks only findings. The design's vector fixes worked-again and carried-over exactly, and this does not change either. Moved words also include results and cell values from before earlier changes (from the replaced-page chain and the sheet's history), so a finding that still says 3 W after a second change is not called carried over.

Home Demo's 'three elements' are taken as the § 12(c) rule's two needs and one unless, as S6's smoke wrote them. 'The right passage' is the paragraph each element's quote is pinned from: § 12(a), § 12(a) and § 12(b).

references.search returns whole PDF pages as passages, so places.py cuts each page into numbered paragraphs itself and ranks those. The words a question's shape adds come from a fixed six-row table (ASKS) and are never guessed.
